subject: Post-demo: model shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist and next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the demo and the clear overview of Acme's support automation goals. Quick recap and a recommended model shortlist so we can get the evals moving:

Top requirements we heard
- Use case: customer support triage + short form generative responses (templates + minor rewriting)
- Latency target: p95 <= 400ms for single-request flows
- Cost target (per token): target below $0.005/token for unit economics at scale
- Quality: intent classification >= 92% on your labeled prompt set; low hallucination for product details
- Constraints: on-prem deployment optional later; need SOC2 evidence and audit logs (we'll include that)

Initial recommended shortlist (tradeoffs included)
1) Llama-3-22B (8-bit quantized) — Balanced quality / latency
   - Rationale: highest overall comprehension on instruction-heavy prompts; expected best quality for edge-case customer phrasing.
   - Estimated perf: p95 ~ 320-380ms (optimized batching + KV cache), cost ~ $0.0025/token (est).
   - Risk: larger memory footprint, needs careful quantization and batch tuning.

2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4/x8) — Cost-efficient, low-latency
   - Rationale: excellent throughput for short responses; very cost-effective for high-volume routing/classification.
   - Estimated perf: p95 ~ 160-220ms, cost ~ $0.0007/token.
   - Risk: slightly lower recall on very long or ambiguous prompts; may need prompt engineering.

3) OpenLlama-13B (fine-tuned) — Quality-forward midpoint
   - Rationale: good quality with smaller latency penalty than larger 22B; good candidate if you want higher baseline quality without 22B cost.
   - Estimated perf: p95 ~ 380-450ms, cost ~ $0.0018/token.

Next steps we recommend
- We'll share a short prompt set + bench results (attached) so you can run the same evals locally.
- Please pick two models from the shortlist to run A/B evaluations on (we suggest Mistral-7B + Llama-3-22B).
- We'll provision a short-term Dedicated instance to run latency tests on your traffic profile (if you want we can mirror a subset of traffic).
- Mutual action plan + timeline attached (has checkpoints for eval, security questionnaire, POC).

Attached: acme-prompt-set-v1.json, redwood-acme-benchmarks-20260830.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the benchmarks and answer questions — available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Dev — quick internal notes to surface before we send artifacts to Acme: 

- Latency assumptions: the numbers Marissa shared are from our internal benches on A10G and A100 flavors with optimized kernels + batching. Cold-start single-stream p95 will be higher for the 22B model (~420-480ms) unless we enable persistent KV caching or warmed worker pools. We should call that out explicitly in the runbook.
- Mistral-7B (q4): p95 single-stream ~180ms on A10G with default runtime batching; cost estimate (in Redwood Dedicated) ~ $0.0007/token (1k tokens =~ $0.70).
- Llama-3-22B (8-bit quant): p95 warmed ~330ms, cold-start ~460ms; cost estimate ~ $0.0025/token (1k tokens =~ $2.50).
- OpenLlama-13B (fine-tuned): p95 ~400ms warmed, cost ~ $0.0018/token.

Ask: when we share the benchmark PDF, include both warmed and cold-start rows and a column with hardware spec. I can attach a short table if you want. Also recommend adding a note about expected variance with aggressive batching (latency vs throughput tradeoff).

I'll prepare the small runbook for Sarah that includes the exact flags we used (quant settings, batch sizes, trace commands) and paste it into the Drive folder.

—Rishi

Model shortlist — concise rationale & recommended eval focus

1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4) — recommended first pass   - Tradeoff: lowest latency and cost; best for high-volume classification and short generative templates.   - Eval focus: run intent-classification recall/precision on your labeled set, and sample generation for templated responses.   - Recommended config: q4/x8, batch size 8 for throughput testing; single-stream p95 target < 220ms (warmed).

2) Llama-3-22B (8-bit quant) — recommended quality baseline   - Tradeoff: highest quality on instruction-heavy and ambiguous prompts; higher cost and memory.   - Eval focus: edge-case prompts, low-signal customer messages, hallucination checks.   - Recommended config: 8-bit quant, persistent warmed workers or small cache TTL to keep cold-starts < 500ms.

3) OpenLlama-13B (fine-tuned) — if you want middle ground   - Tradeoff: better quality than 7B with less overhead than 22B.   - Eval focus: A/B for mid-length prompts and throughput vs cost analysis.

Suggested timeline- Today: we shared artifacts and runbook (attached).- By Fri (2026-09-03): Acme to run evals on two models (we recommend Mistral-7B + Llama-3-22B).- Next Tue (2026-09-07): Joint results review + decision on POC config + Dedicated short-term provision.

Let me know which two models you want us to spin up for the short Dedicated trial and we'll provision. Also — Rishi will drop the runbook into the Drive in the next hour.

Best,
